newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks close higher, buying frenzy slows.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks close higher, buying frenzy slows.

text.p: ** (1230 GMT) Shares finish up, seen holding ground
** Budget seen widely accepted, helps political
stability-traders
** Pro-market budget-triggered buying slows
** UBS Securities says "overweight" on Indian stocks,
Banque Paribas goes "neutral" from "buy"
** Benchmark Bombay index rises 73.56 points to 3,944.61,
National exchange index gains 9.6 points to 1,117.30,
Delhi index adds 13.32 points to 837.05
Shares across India finished higher on Tuesday after a market friendly budget was seen helping political stability, brokers said.

"The budget has been applauded by industrialists, the markets and the common man," said Vijay Pandya, director at Classic Share and Stock Brokers. "It has given new confidence in the government...its tenure looks secure."

The 15-party coalition of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda won a crucial vote in parliament on Tuesday, garnering support from its reluctant Congress party ally for government policies spelt out by President Shankar Dayal Sharma last month.
Gowda's United Front alliance controls fewer than 200 seats in the 545-member house, but it has the support of the Congress party's 140 deputies.
Deve Gowda's government elected to office last May may complete its five-year term, traders said.
"Easing liquidity and the abolition of tax on dividend income has significantly increased the attractiveness of investments in equities," UBS Securities said.
"We expect the stock market to rerate strongly as investors shift from debt to equities."
But the international equity research division of Banque Paribas cautioned investors as it saw the market overheated.
"We think the improvements overall are relatively small to have generated a 14 percent rise in the index in three days," it said. "We are getting nervous."
The BSE hit 4,007.91 intraday high on Monday before closing at 3,871.05 -- against 3,474.79 in pre-budget trade on Friday.
Foreign funds were buyers after the 1997/98 (April-March) raised foreign portfolio investment limits to 30 percent from 24 percent, Delhi brokers said.
The National bourse's Midcap index closed 4.13 points lower at 1,166.43 due to business-squaring on the last day of weekly account, traders said.
--RANJIT GANGADHARAN, Bombay Equities +91-22-265-9000
